tools.name: os3d
tools.title: OpenShape 3D
tools.description: Everything in OpenShape 3D goes through this one tool, so the person approves it once. op names the operation and args carries its arguments (os3d.guide lists them all with units, axes and recipes; read it once before modelling). READS: 'health' (is the app reachable, is a design open — call first), 'guide' (the modelling guide), 'state' (every body with exact volume in mm3 and bounds, selection, undo state — verify geometry here, not in a picture), 'faces' and 'edges' with args {"body": id} (1-based kernel indices that shell, fillet, chamfer and the face ops take; re-list after every feature), 'sketches', 'check' with optional {"body", "bop": true} (is it a valid solid — run before exporting), 'screenshot' with optional {"width", "height"} (a JPEG of the viewport; wait a second after a view command), 'commands' (runnable command ids). CHANGES, each recorded as an undoable feature exactly as if modelled by hand: 'sketch.create', 'sketch.addEntities', 'feature.extrude', 'feature.revolve', 'feature.loft', 'feature.sweep', 'feature.shell', 'feature.fillet', 'feature.chamfer', 'feature.boolean', 'feature.pattern', 'feature.mirror', 'feature.transform', 'feature.pushPull', the face ops, 'body.setMaterial', 'item.setHidden'; 'command.run' with {"id": "view.fit"} runs a view or undo/redo command (edit.undo reverts one feature); 'document.export' with {"format": "stl"|"3mf"|"obj"|"step", "up": "z", "body": [ids], "name": "flowerpot"} saves a file to the person's Downloads folder (up='z' for a 3D-printing slicer; one printable part per file; the reply gives fileName, path and sizeMM). Units are millimetres and degrees. A feature reply carries the new state plus producedBodyIDs / changedBodyIDs / removedBodyIDs; 'failed': true means the feature was recorded but did not build — read 'message', run command.run edit.undo, and correct the arguments.

op.description: Operation name: health, guide, state, faces, edges, sketches, check, screenshot, commands, or a change such as feature.extrude, command.run, document.export.

args.description: The operation's arguments (omit for health, guide, state, sketches, commands).
